{{DISPLAYTITLE:''A priori'' estimate}}
In the theory of [[partial differential equation]]s, an '''''a priori'' estimate''' (also called an '''apriori estimate''' or '''''a priori'' bound''') is an estimate for the size of a solution or its derivatives of a partial differential equation. ''A priori'' is Latin for "from before" and refers to the fact that the estimate for the solution is derived before the solution is known to exist. One reason for their importance is that if one can prove an ''a priori'' estimate for solutions of a differential equation, then it is often possible to prove that solutions exist using the [[continuity method]] or a [[fixed point theorem]].

''A priori'' estimates were introduced and named by [[Sergei Natanovich Bernstein]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Bernstein |first=Serge |date=June 1906 |title=Sur la generalisation du probleme de Dirichlet: Premiere partie |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/BF01449980 |journal=Mathematische Annalen |language=fr |volume=62 |issue=2 |pages=253–271 |doi=10.1007/BF01449980 |issn=0025-5831}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Bernstein |first=Serge |date=March 1910 |title=Sur la generalisation du probleme de Dirichlet: Deuxième partie |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/BF01455154 |journal=Mathematische Annalen |language=fr |volume=69 |issue=1 |pages=82–136 |doi=10.1007/BF01455154 |issn=0025-5831|url-access=subscription }}</ref> who used them to prove existence of solutions to  second order nonlinear [[Elliptic partial differential equation|elliptic equations]] in the plane. Some other early influential examples of ''a priori'' estimates include the [[Schauder estimates]] given by [[Juliusz Schauder]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Schauder |first=J. |date=December 1934 |title=Über lineare elliptische Differentialgleichungen zweiter Ordnung. |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/BF01170635 |journal=Mathematische Zeitschrift |language=de |volume=38 |issue=1 |pages=257–282 |doi=10.1007/BF01170635 |issn=0025-5874|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Citation |last=Schauder |first=Juliusz |title=Numerische Abschätzungen in elliptischen linearen Differentialgleichungen |periodical=Studia Mathematica |volume=5 |issue= |pages=34–42 |year=1937 |url=http://matwbn.icm.edu.pl/ksiazki/sm/sm5/sm516.pdf |location=Lwów, Poland |publisher=Polska Akademia Nauk. Instytut Matematyczny |language=German |author-link=Juliusz Schauder}}</ref> and the estimates given by De Giorgi and Nash for second order elliptic or [[parabolic equation]]s in many variables, in their respective solutions to [[Hilbert's nineteenth problem]].
